title: Validity and reliability of SEIS-3 for measuring strength in older adults
author: Sobral-Monteiro-Junior, Coutinho, et al.
materials: was developed, consisting of three scores: (

steps.title: Set up dynamometer and participant
steps.instruction: Place the digital dynamometer (DM‑90, Itest, Bosque da Saúde, São Paulo, Brazil) on a stable surface and seat the participant comfortably with both hands ready to grip.

steps.title: Familiarize participant with grip test
steps.instruction: Allow the participant to practice gripping the dynamometer until comfortable, without recording any data.

steps.title: Measure maximal isometric grip (MIVC)
steps.instruction: Instruct the participant to grip the dynamometer with each hand and exert a maximal isometric voluntary contraction for five seconds; record the peak force (kgf) for each hand.

steps.title: Assess SEIS‑3 effort levels
steps.instruction: Present the three SEIS‑3 categories (Light, Moderate, Strong) in a randomly assigned order; for each category, ask the participant to grip the dynamometer at the indicated subjective effort and record the force (kgf).

steps.title: Repeat assessment after rest
steps.instruction: Allow a 10‑minute rest period, then repeat the SEIS‑3 assessment (steps 3‑4) using the same random order of effort levels.

steps.title: Calculate effort percentages
steps.instruction: For each SEIS‑3 effort level, divide the recorded force (kgf) by the participant’s MIVC (kgf) and express the result as a percentage of MIVC.

steps.title: Perform statistical analyses

substeps.instruction: Conduct linear regression of effort‑level forces versus MIVC to obtain R².
Calculate the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) to assess test‑retest reliability.
Generate Bland‑Altman plots to evaluate 95 % agreement across time points.
